Response Text:---
I looked through the codebase and didn’t find any other hints or tests for `distance()`, so the only guidance we have is the Javadoc:

> “Hint: The value of `currentValue` will roll into negative once the delay ends. You may use the absolute value of this number to compute the number of valid moves since the delay has ended.”【F:game/DelayBar.java†L12-L21】

From that, the semantics of `distance()` should be:

1. **While** the delay is still counting down (`currentValue > 0`), the water hasn’t started flowing, so the distance is `0`.
2. **Once** the countdown has passed (i.e. `currentValue <= 0`), the water flows forward.  On the very first “tick” after reaching zero, `currentValue` will be `0`, and thereafter it becomes negative.  The absolute value of that (`|currentValue|`) is exactly how many rounds have elapsed since the delay ended, so that should be the distance.

Putting that into code gives the following implementation of `distance()`.

---

```java
package game;

import util.StringUtils;

/**
 * Class representing the delay before the water starts to flow in the map.
 */
class DelayBar {

    private final int initialValue;
    private int currentValue;

    /**
     * Constructs a {@link DelayBar}.
     *
     * @param initialValue Number of rounds to wait before the water starts to flow.
     */
    DelayBar(int initialValue) {
        this.initialValue = initialValue;
        this.currentValue = initialValue;
    }

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: The value of {@code currentValue} will roll into negative once the delay ends. You may use the absolute
     * value of this number to compute the number of valid moves since the delay has ended.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return The distance the water should flow at this stage.
     */
    int distance() {
        // If we're still in the countdown (currentValue > 0), no flow yet.
        if (currentValue > 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        // Once currentValue <= 0, use the absolute number of rounds since delay ended.
        return Math.abs(currentValue);
    }

    void display() {
        if (currentValue > 0) {
            System.out.print("Rounds Countdown: ");
            System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(currentValue, '='));
            System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(initialValue - currentValue, ' '));
            System.out.print(" " + currentValue);
            System.out.println();
        } else {
            System.out.println();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Decrements the current value by 1.
     */
    void countdown() {
        currentValue--;
    }
}
```
【F:game/DelayBar.java†L1-L75】

---

**Explanation in brief**  
- **Before** the delay ends (`currentValue > 0`): return `0` (water hasn’t started).  
- **After** the delay ends (`currentValue <= 0`): return `|currentValue|`, i.e. how many ticks have passed since the countdown hit zero.  

This fulfills the Javadoc’s hint and lets the water flow forward by one additional unit each round once the delay has elapsed.

package game;

import util.StringUtils;

/**
 * Class representing the delay before the water starts to flow in the map.

class DelayBar {

    private final int initialValue;
    private int currentValue;

    /**
     * Constructs a {@link DelayBar}.
     *
     * @param initialValue Number of rounds to wait before the water starts to flow.
     */
    DelayBar(int initialValue) {
        this.initialValue = initialValue;
        this.currentValue = initialValue;
    }

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: The value of {@code currentValue} will roll into negative once the delay ends. You may use the absolute
     * value of this number to compute the number of valid moves since the delay has ended.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return The distance the water should flow at this stage.
     */
    int distance() {
        // If we're still in the countdown (currentValue > 0), no flow yet.
        if (currentValue > 0) {
            return 0;
        }
        // Once currentValue <= 0, use the absolute number of rounds since delay ended.
        return Math.abs(currentValue);
    }

    void display() {
        if (currentValue > 0) {
            System.out.print("Rounds Countdown: ");
            System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(currentValue, '='));
            System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(initialValue - currentValue, ' '));
            System.out.print(" " + currentValue);
            System.out.println();
        } else {
            System.out.println();
        }
    }

    /**
     * Decrements the current value by 1.
     */
    void countdown() {
        currentValue--;
    }

Response Text:---
Below is an implementation of `Game.placePipe(int row, char col)` that converts the 1‑based row/column into a `Coordinate`, tries to place the pipe on the map, and—if successful—advances the pipe queue, delay bar and cell stack, and increments the step counter.

```java
/**
 * Places a pipe at (row, col).
 *
 * <p>
 * This method should convert the row and column into {@link Coordinate} and try to place the pipe on the map. If
 * this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param row Row number, 1-based.
 * @param col Column character.
 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed.
 */
public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
    // convert 1-based row and lettered column into a Coordinate
    Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'A');
    // attempt to place the next pipe from the queue onto the map
    Pipe next = pipeQueue.peek();
    if (!map.placePipe(coord, next)) {
        return false;
    }
    // on success: consume the pipe, record the cell and delay, bump steps
    pipeQueue.poll();
    cellStack.push(coord, next);
    delayBar.advance();
    numOfSteps++;
    return true;
}
```
【F:game/Game.java†L41-L61】

**Explanation**  
1. **Coordinate conversion**: Translates the 1‑based row and lettered column into zero‑based indices via `new Coordinate(row-1, col-'A')`.  
2. **Place on map**: Peeks the next `Pipe` from `pipeQueue` and calls `map.placePipe(...)`.  
3. **On success**:  
   - Removes the used pipe from `pipeQueue` (`poll()`).  
   - Pushes the placed pipe and its location onto `cellStack` for undo capability.  
   - Advances the `delayBar`.  
   - Increments `numOfSteps`.  
4. Returns `true` only if the pipe placement succeeds, otherwise `false`.

 * Places a pipe at (row, col).

    // convert 1-based row and lettered column into a Coordinate

Response Text:---
Here is one possible implementation of `skipPipe()` in `Game` that simply skips (discards) the current pipe and advances to the next one in the pipe queue, while counting that action as a step (so `numOfSteps` is incremented) and advancing the delay bar just as if the player had placed a pipe:

```java
/**
 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
 */
public void skipPipe() {
    pipeQueue.poll();    // remove/discard the current pipe
    delayBar.advance();  // count it as one "round"
    numOfSteps++;        // increment the step counter
}
```
【F:game/Game.java†L34-L41】

**Explanation:**
- `pipeQueue.poll()` removes the head pipe so the next pipe becomes available.
- `delayBar.advance()` simulates the passing of one round when skipping.
- `numOfSteps++` treats the skip as a step taken by the player.

Response Text:---
It looks like the implementation of `undoStep()` depends on how your undo stack is represented and what each undo step must reverse. In your project you have a `CellStack` to record placed pipes (coordinates + pipe) and you need to undo the most recent placement by:

1. Checking whether the stack is empty (nothing to undo → return `false`).
2. Popping the last move off the `cellStack`.
3. Removing the pipe from the map at that coordinate.
4. Pushing the pipe back onto the front of the `pipeQueue`.
5. Resetting the delay bar (i.e. rolling back one “advance”).
6. Incrementing the step counter (undoing counts as a step).
7. Returning `true`.

Below is a concise implementation of `undoStep()` that follows those rules. 

```java
/**
 * Undos a step from the game.
 *
 * <p>
 * Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code false} if there are no steps to undo, otherwise {@code true}.
 */
public boolean undoStep() {
    if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
        return false;
    }
    var entry = cellStack.pop();
    Coordinate coord = entry.coordinate();
    Pipe pipe = entry.pipe();

    map.clearPipe(coord);      // remove pipe from map
    pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);  // put the pipe back at the front of the queue
    delayBar.rewind();         // undo the last delay advance
    numOfSteps++;              // undoing counts as a step

    return true;
}
```

```java
 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow.
 *
 * <p>
 * This method should invoke {@link Map#fillTiles(int)} up to a certain distance.
 * </p>
 */
public void updateState() {
    // How far water can flow this turn:
    int flowDistance = delayBar.get();      // number of rounds to wait before filling
    for (int d = 1; d <= flowDistance; d++) {
        map.fillTiles(d);
    }
    // After filling, rewind the delay bar so that next round starts over:
    delayBar.rewind();
}
```

- Finally, we rewind the delay bar to reset its countdown for the next round.

This satisfies the requirement to “invoke `Map.fillTiles(int)` up to a certain distance.”

```java
import game.map.Map;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**

		map.display();
		System.out.println();

		cellStack.display();

	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.

	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows   Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'A');
		Pipe next = pipeQueue.peek();
		if (!map.placePipe(coord, next)) {
			return false;
		}
		pipeQueue.poll();
		cellStack.push(coord, next);
		delayBar.advance();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.poll();
		delayBar.advance();
		numOfSteps++;
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		var entry = cellStack.pop();
		Coordinate coord = entry.coordinate();
		Pipe pipe = entry.pipe();
		map.clearPipe(coord);
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
		delayBar.rewind();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}
```

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
```java
		int flowDistance = delayBar.get();
		for (int d = 1; d <= flowDistance; d++) {
			map.fillTiles(d);
		}
		delayBar.rewind();
	}
```

```java
	boolean isFull();
}
```

Below is one correct proposal for the revised `Game` class that restores the intended constructors (removing the spurious `void`), adds the two‐arg constructor, and implements `hasLost()` and `hasWon()` in accordance with the hints and the rest of the API.  With this in place, your JUnit5 tests in `GameTest` and `MainTest` should compile and pass.

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

    @NotNull
    private final Map map;
    @NotNull
    private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
    @NotNull
    private final DelayBar delayBar;
    @NotNull
    private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

    private int numOfSteps = 0;

    /**
     * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
     *
     * <p>
     * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows    Number of rows of the given map.
     * @param cols    Number of columns of the given map.
     * @param delay   Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
     * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
     * @param pipes   List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
     * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
     */
    @NotNull
    public static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
        var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);
        return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
    }

    /**
     * Quick‐start constructor for the main game loop.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols) {
        this(rows, cols, /* default delay */ 1, Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, Map.defaultMapString(rows, cols)), /* no pipes */ null);
    }

    /**
     * Full constructor.
     *
     * @param rows   Number of rows of the map.
     * @param cols   Number of columns of the map.
     * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
     * @param cells  Cells of the map.
     * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
        this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
        this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
    }

    /**
     * Displays the current game state.
     */
    public void display() {
        map.display();
        System.out.println();
        pipeQueue.display();
        cellStack.display();
        System.out.println();
        delayBar.display();
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game is lost.
     *
     * <p>
     * A loss occurs if the map reports a loss.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        return map.hasLost();
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game is won.
     *
     * <p>
     * A win occurs if the map is completely filled.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code true} if the game is won.
     */
    public boolean hasWon() {
        return map.isFull();
    }

    /**
     * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
     */
    public int getNumOfSteps() {
        return numOfSteps;
    }

    /**
     * Places a pipe at (row, col).
     * <p>
     *  This method should convert the row and column into {@link Coordinate} and try to place the pipe on the map.
     *  If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param row Row number, 1-based.
     * @param col Column character.
     * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed.
     */
    public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
        Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'A');
        Pipe next = pipeQueue.peek();
        if (!map.placePipe(coord, next)) {
            return false;
        }
        pipeQueue.poll();
        cellStack.push(coord, next);
        delayBar.advance();
        numOfSteps++;
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
     */
    public void skipPipe() {
        pipeQueue.poll();
        delayBar.advance();
        numOfSteps++;
    }

    /**
     * Undos a step from the game.
     * <p>
     *  Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one.
     * </p>
     * <p>
     *  Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code false} if there are no steps to undo, otherwise {@code true}.
     */
    public boolean undoStep() {
        if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
            return false;
        }
        var entry = cellStack.pop();
        Coordinate coord = entry.coordinate();
        Pipe pipe = entry.pipe();
        map.clearPipe(coord);
        pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
        delayBar.rewind();
        numOfSteps++;
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow.
     * <p>
     *  This method should invoke {@link Map#fillTiles(int)} up to a certain distance.
     * </p>
     */
    public void updateState() {
        int flowDistance = delayBar.get();
        for (int d = 1; d <= flowDistance; d++) {
            map.fillTiles(d);
        }
        delayBar.rewind();
    }

    /**
     * @return {@code true} if the map is fully filled (winning condition).
     */
    public boolean isFull() {
        return map.isFull();
    }
}
```

3. **Implemented** `hasLost()` to delegate to `map.hasLost()`, and **added** `hasWon()` for the winning check.
4. Ensured `getNumOfSteps()` simply returns the `numOfSteps` field.

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

	@NotNull
	private final Map map;
	@NotNull
	private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
	@NotNull
	private final DelayBar delayBar;
	@NotNull
	private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

	private int numOfSteps = 0;

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current game state.
	 */
	public void display() {
		map.display();
		System.out.println();
		pipeQueue.display();
		cellStack.display();
		System.out.println();
		delayBar.display();
	}

	/**
	 * Checks whether the game is lost.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: This method should invoke {@link Map#hasLost()}. You may also need other judgements.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
	 */
	public boolean hasLost() {
		// TODO
		return false;
	}

	/**
	 * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
	 */
	public int getNumOfSteps() {
		// TODO
		return 0;
	}

	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
	 * @param rows   Number of rows of the given map.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns of the given map.
	 * @param delay  Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
	 * @param cells  Cells of the map.
	 * @param pipes  List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
	 */
	public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
		this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
		this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
		this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
	}

	/**
	 * Places a pipe at (row, col). <p> This method should convert the row and column into  {@link Coordinate}  and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps. </p>
	 * @param row  Row number, 1-based.
	 * @param col  Column character.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed.
	 */
	public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
		Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'A');
		Pipe next = pipeQueue.peek();
		if (!map.placePipe(coord, next)) {
			return false;
		}
		pipeQueue.poll();
		cellStack.push(coord, next);
		delayBar.advance();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
	 */
	public void skipPipe() {
		pipeQueue.poll();
		delayBar.advance();
		numOfSteps++;
	}

	/**
	 * Undos a step from the game. <p> Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo. </p>
	 * @return   {@code  false}  if there are no steps to undo, otherwise  {@code  true} .
	 */
	public boolean undoStep() {
		if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
			return false;
		}
		var entry = cellStack.pop();
		Coordinate coord = entry.coordinate();
		Pipe pipe = entry.pipe();
		map.clearPipe(coord);
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
		delayBar.rewind();
		numOfSteps++;
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according to the distance the water should flow. <p> This method should invoke  {@link Map#fillTiles(int)}  up to a certain distance. </p>
	 */
	public void updateState() {
		int flowDistance = delayBar.get();
		for (int d = 1; d <= flowDistance; d++) {
			map.fillTiles(d);
		}
		delayBar.rewind();
	}

	boolean isFull();
}
```

#### Explanation

- In your current `Game.java` you wrote
  ```java
  public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) { … }
  public void Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) { … }
  ```
  but because they have a return type (`void`), those are _methods_, _not_ constructors.  Hence the test’s calls to `new Game(...)` cannot find any matching constructors.
- By converting them into real constructors (i.e. remove the return type), you provide the expected signatures.
- Likewise, `Main` expects a two‐argument constructor `Game(int,int)` and a `hasWon()` method.

Below is the fixed `Game.java`.  (No other classes are touched.)

```java
package game;

import game.map.Map;
import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;
import util.Coordinate;

import java.util.List;

public class Game {

    @NotNull
    private final Map map;
    @NotNull
    private final PipeQueue pipeQueue;
    @NotNull
    private final DelayBar delayBar;
    @NotNull
    private final CellStack cellStack = new CellStack();

    private int numOfSteps = 0;

    /**
     * Creates a game with a given map and various properties.
     *
     * <p>
     * This constructor is a convenience method for unit testing purposes.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows Number of rows of the given map.
     * @param cols Number of columns of the given map.
     * @param delay Delay in number of rounds before filling the pipes.
     * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
     * @param pipes List of pre-generated pipes, if any.
     * @return A game constructed with the given parameters.
     */
    @NotNull
    static Game fromString(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
        var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);
        return new Game(rows, cols, delay, cells, pipes);
    }

    /**
     * Displays the current game state.
     */
    public void display() {
        map.display();
        System.out.println();
        pipeQueue.display();
        cellStack.display();
        System.out.println();
        delayBar.display();
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game is lost.
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: This method should invoke {@link Map#hasLost()}. You may also need other judgements.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
     */
    public boolean hasLost() {
        return map.hasLost() || delayBar.isOverflown();
    }

    /**
     * Checks whether the game is won.
     *
     * @return {@code true} if the player filled all fillable tiles.
     */
    public boolean hasWon() {
        return map.isFilled();
    }

    /**
     * @return Number of steps the player has taken.
     */
    public int getNumOfSteps() {
        return numOfSteps;
    }

    /**
     * Core constructor taking an existing cell‐array and pipe list.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, Cell[][] cells, List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this.map = new Map(rows, cols, cells);
        this.pipeQueue = new PipeQueue(pipes);
        this.delayBar = new DelayBar(delay);
    }

    /**
     * Convenience constructor taking a String map representation.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols, int delay, @NotNull String cellsRep, @Nullable List<Pipe> pipes) {
        this(rows, cols, delay, Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep), pipes);
    }

    /**
     * Two‐argument constructor used by Main for interactive play.
     */
    public Game(int rows, int cols) {
        this(rows, cols, DelayBar.DEFAULT_DELAY, new Cell[rows][cols], /*pipes=*/null);
    }

    /**
     * Places a pipe at (row, col).
     *
     * <p>
     * This method should convert the row and column into {@link Coordinate}
     * and try to place the pipe on the map. If this succeeds, also update
     * the pipe queue, delay bar, cell stack, and the number of steps.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param row Row number, 1-based.
     * @param col Column character.
     * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed.
     */
    public boolean placePipe(int row, char col) {
        Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(row - 1, col - 'A');
        Pipe next = pipeQueue.peek();
        if (!map.placePipe(coord, next)) {
            return false;
        }
        pipeQueue.poll();
        cellStack.push(coord, next);
        delayBar.advance();
        numOfSteps++;
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Directly skips the current pipe and use the next pipe.
     */
    public void skipPipe() {
        pipeQueue.poll();
        delayBar.advance();
        numOfSteps++;
    }

    /**
     * Undos a step from the game.
     *
     * <p>
     * Note: Undoing a step counts will increment the number of steps by one.
     * </p>
     *
     * <p>
     * Hint: Remember to check whether there are cells to undo.
     * </p>
     *
     * @return {@code false} if there are no steps to undo, otherwise {@code true}.
     */
    public boolean undoStep() {
        if (cellStack.isEmpty()) {
            return false;
        }
        var entry = cellStack.pop();
        Coordinate coord = entry.coordinate();
        Pipe pipe = entry.pipe();
        map.clearPipe(coord);
        pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
        delayBar.rewind();
        numOfSteps++;
        return true;
    }

    /**
     * Updates the game state. More specifically, it fills pipes according
     * to the distance the water should flow.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method should invoke {@link Map#fillTiles(int)} up to a certain distance.
     * </p>
     */
    public void updateState() {
        int flowDistance = delayBar.get();
        for (int d = 1; d <= flowDistance; d++) {
            map.fillTiles(d);
        }
        delayBar.rewind();
    }

    boolean isFull() {
        return map.isFilled();
    }
}
```

```java
package game;

import game.pipes.Pipe;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.LinkedList;
import java.util.List;

class PipeQueue {

    private static final int MAX_GEN_LENGTH = 5;

    @NotNull
    private final LinkedList<Pipe> pipeQueue;

    /**
     * Creates a pipe queue with pipes already filled in the queue. Ultimately, it should contain
     * {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} number of pipes.
     *
     * <p>
     * This method should also populate the queue until it has {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} number of pipes in it.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param pipes List of pipes to display before generated pipes.
     */
    PipeQueue(List<Pipe> pipes) {
        // 1. Initialize the internal LinkedList
        this.pipeQueue = new LinkedList<>();

        // 2. Add all user‑provided pipes first (up to MAX_GEN_LENGTH)
        for (Pipe p : pipes) {
            if (pipeQueue.size() >= MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
                break;
            }
            pipeQueue.add(p);
        }

        // 3. Fill in with randomly generated pipes until we reach MAX_GEN_LENGTH
        while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
            pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
        }
    }

    // ... other methods (peek, consume, undo, display, generateNewPipe) ...
}
```

Response Text:---
Below is a simple, self‐contained implementation of the `undo` method that pushes the given `pipe` back onto the front of the queue and then trims the end of the queue (if necessary) so that the overall queue length never exceeds `MAX_GEN_LENGTH`. This restores the queue to what it was immediately prior to the last “consume” (or any other operation that removed the front pipe).

```java
/**
 * Undoes a step by inserting {@code pipe} into the front of the queue.
 *
 * @param pipe Pipe to insert to front of queue.
 */
void undo(final Pipe pipe) {
    // Put the undone pipe back at the head of the queue
    pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
    // If re‐inserting makes the queue too long, drop the last pipe
    if (pipeQueue.size() > MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
        pipeQueue.removeLast();
    }
}
```

Explanation:

1. **Insert at front**  
   We use `LinkedList.addFirst(pipe)` to re‑insert the undone pipe at the head of the queue.
2. **Maintain constant length**  
   Since `MAX_GEN_LENGTH` is the fixed capacity of our visible queue, if re‑inserting pushes us over that limit, we simply drop the tail (`removeLast()`) so the size remains exactly `MAX_GEN_LENGTH`.

This satisfies the contract “Undoes a step by inserting `pipe` into the front of the queue,” while keeping the queue exactly `MAX_GEN_LENGTH` long.

```java
			pipeQueue.add(generateNewPipe());
		}
```

```java
	 * Peeks the next pipe.
	 * @return  The next pipe in the queue.
	 * @throws IllegalStateException  if there are no pipes in the queue.
	 */
	Pipe peek() {
		if (pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("No pipes in the queue.");
		}
		return pipeQueue.getFirst();
	}

	/**
	 * Consumes the next pipe. This method removes the pipe from the queue, and generate new ones if the queue has less elements than {@link PipeQueue#MAX_GEN_LENGTH} .
	 */
	void consume() {
		if (pipeQueue.isEmpty()) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("No pipes to consume.");
		}
		pipeQueue.removeFirst();
		while (pipeQueue.size() < MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
			pipeQueue.addLast(generateNewPipe());
		}
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step by inserting  {@code  pipe}  into the front of the queue.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to insert to front of queue.
	 */
	void undo(final Pipe pipe) {
		pipeQueue.addFirst(pipe);
		if (pipeQueue.size() > MAX_GEN_LENGTH) {
			pipeQueue.removeLast();
		}
	}
```

Below is one correct implementation of that constructor.  It uses the existing helper methods `generateStartCellInfo()` and `generateEndCellInfo()`, and the cell‐factory methods on `TerminationCell`, `Wall`, and `FillableCell`.

```java
/**
 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols.
 *
 * <p>
 * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
 * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
 * The source tile must not point into a wall.
 * The sink tile must point outside the map.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param rows Number of rows.
 * @param cols Number of columns.
 */
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
    if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");
    }
    this.rows = rows;
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];

    // First fill everything with walls on the border, fillable cells inside
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
            if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
                cells[r][c] = new Wall();
            } else {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
            }
        }
    }

    // Place exactly one source (inside, pointing inward)
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo startInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
    this.sourceCell = TerminationCell.createSource(startInfo.coord, startInfo.direction);
    cells[startInfo.coord.row][startInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;

    // Place exactly one sink (on the edge, pointing outward)
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo endInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
    this.sinkCell = TerminationCell.createSink(endInfo.coord, endInfo.direction);
    cells[endInfo.coord.row][endInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
}
```

**Explanation (brief):**
1. **Validate size**: We require at least 3×3 so there is interior space to place a non‐edge source.
2. **Initialize fields** (`rows`, `cols`, `cells`).
3. **Fill the grid**:
   - Border cells (row 0 or row rows-1, col 0 or col cols-1) → `Wall`
   - Interior cells → `FillableCell`
4. **Pick and place the source** by calling `generateStartCellInfo()` (which returns a random non‐edge coordinate and a valid inward‐pointing direction), then use `TerminationCell.createSource(...)` and overwrite that cell.
5. **Pick and place the sink** similarly using `generateEndCellInfo()` and `TerminationCell.createSink(...)`.

This satisfies the requirements: exactly one source in a non‐edge cell, one sink on the edge, with proper pointing constraints.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}
```

```java
 * Map of the game.

public class Map {

    private final int rows;
    private final int cols;
    @NotNull
    final Cell[][] cells;

    private TerminationCell sourceCell;
    private TerminationCell sinkCell;

    @NotNull
    private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
    private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
    private Integer prevFilledDistance;

    /**
     * Creates a map with the given cells.
     *
     * <p>
     * The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell.
     * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
     * The source tile must not point into a wall.
     * The sink tile must point outside the map.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows  Number of rows.
     * @param cols  Number of columns.
     * @param cells Cells to fill the map.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");
        }
        if (cells.length != rows) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells.length != rows");
        }
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            if (cells[r].length != cols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells[" + r + "].length != cols");
            }
        }

        this.rows = rows;
        this.cols = cols;
        this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];

        TerminationCell foundSource = null;
        TerminationCell foundSink = null;

        // scan the supplied cells for source and sink; copy into our array
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
                Cell cell = cells[r][c];
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tcell) {
                    if (tcell.isSource()) {
                        if (foundSource != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
                        }
                        // source must be in non-edge
                        if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source tile must not be on edge");
                        }
                        // source must not point into a wall
                        Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols ||
                            cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into wall or outside map");
                        }
                        foundSource = tcell;
                        this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
                    } else {
                        // sink
                        if (foundSink != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
                        }
                        // sink must be on edge
                        if (r != 0 && r != rows - 1 && c != 0 && c != cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink tile must be on edge");
                        }
                        // sink must point outside map
                        Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (adj.row >= 0 && adj.row < rows && adj.col >= 0 && adj.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink points into map");
                        }
                        foundSink = tcell;
                        this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
                    }
                } else {
                    this.cells[r][c] = cell;
                }
            }
        }

        if (foundSource == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
        }
        if (foundSink == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
        }

        this.sourceCell = foundSource;
        this.sinkCell = foundSink;
    }
```

**Explanation of key steps:**

1. **Argument validation**  
   - Ensure `rows` and `cols` are at least 3×3.  
   - Ensure the provided `cells` array dimensions match `rows`×`cols`.

2. **Scanning for exactly one source and one sink**  
   - Loop through every cell; when encountering a `TerminationCell`, check whether it’s a source or sink.  
   - Enforce “exactly one” of each, throwing an exception if zero or more than one is found.

3. **Location constraints**  
   - The source must lie strictly in a non-edge row/column.  
   - The sink must lie on one of the edge rows/columns.

4. **Direction constraints**  
   - A source’s exit direction must point into an adjacent cell that is not a `Wall` (and within bounds).  
   - A sink’s exit direction must point outside the map (i.e.\ its adjacent coordinate is out of bounds).

5. **Copying the cells**  
   - Fill our internal `this.cells` array with the validated cells (and leave all other cells untouched).

This satisfies the Javadoc requirements and completes the constructor so the map can be built from any valid `Cell[][]` input.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

    /**

     *
```

     * The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell.
     * The source tile must not point into a wall.
     * The sink tile must point outside the map.
     * </p>
     *
     * @param rows  Number of rows.
     * @param cols  Number of columns.
     * @param cells Cells to fill the map.
     */
    public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
        if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");
        }
        if (cells.length != rows) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells.length != rows");
        }
        for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
            if (cells[r].length != cols) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells[" + r + "].length != cols");
            }
        }

        this.cols = cols;

        TerminationCell foundSink = null;

                Cell cell = cells[r][c];
                if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tcell) {
                    if (tcell.isSource()) {
                        if (foundSource != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
                        }
                        // source must be in non-edge
                        if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source tile must not be on edge");
                        }
                        // source must not point into a wall
                        Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols ||
                            cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into wall or outside map");

                        foundSource = tcell;
                        this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
                    } else {
                        // sink
                        if (foundSink != null) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
                        }
                        // sink must be on edge
                        if (r != 0 && r != rows - 1 && c != 0 && c != cols - 1) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink tile must be on edge");
                        }
                        // sink must point outside map
                        Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
                        if (adj.row >= 0 && adj.row < rows && adj.col >= 0 && adj.col < cols) {
                            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink points into map");
                        }
                        foundSink = tcell;
                        this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
                    }
                } else {
                    this.cells[r][c] = cell;
                }
            }
        }

        if (foundSource == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
        }
        if (foundSink == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
        }

        this.sourceCell = foundSource;
        this.sinkCell = foundSink;

Below is a self‑contained implementation of the complete method:

```java
/**
 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
 *
 * <p>
 * Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied.
 * </p>
 * <p>
 * Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a 
 * {@link FillableCell}.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param row One‑Based row number to place pipe at.
 * @param col One‑Based column number to place pipe at.
 * @param p   Pipe to place in cell.
 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
 */
boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
    // Convert to 0-based indices
    int r = row - 1;
    int c = col - 1;
    // Check bounds
    if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
        return false;
    }
    // Only FillableCell can accept a pipe
    Cell cell = cells[r][c];
    if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
        return false;
    }
    // Cannot overwrite an existing pipe
    if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
        return false;
    }
    // Place the pipe
    fillable.setPipe(p);
    return true;
}
```

```java
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.
	 * @param cols  Number of columns.
	 */
	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall();
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo startInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		this.sourceCell = TerminationCell.createSource(startInfo.coord, startInfo.direction);
		cells[startInfo.coord.row][startInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo endInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		this.sinkCell = TerminationCell.createSink(endInfo.coord, endInfo.direction);
		cells[endInfo.coord.row][endInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");
		}
		if (cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells.length != rows");
		}
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			if (cells[r].length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells[" + r + "].length != cols");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tcell) {
					if (tcell.isSource()) {
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
						}
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source tile must not be on edge");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols
								|| cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into wall or outside map");
						}
						foundSource = tcell;
						this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
					} else {
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
						}
						if (r != 0 && r != rows - 1 && c != 0 && c != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink tile must be on edge");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (adj.row >= 0 && adj.row < rows && adj.col >= 0 && adj.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink points into map");
						}
						foundSink = tcell;
						this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
					}
				} else {
					this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}
}
```

Below is one possible implementation of the `undo` method for the `Map` class.  It strictly follows the Javadoc contract:

1. It checks that the target cell is a `FillableCell`, throwing `IllegalArgumentException` otherwise.  
2. It “undoes” the cell at the given coordinate by clearing any pipe on it.  
3. It also updates the bookkeeping for filled tiles (`filledTiles`, `prevFilledTiles`, and `prevFilledDistance`) so that a subsequent call to `fillTiles(...)` will correctly re‑compute the fill state.

```java
/**
 * Undoes a step from the map.
 *
 * <p>
 * Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param coord Coordinate to reset.
 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the cell is not an instance of {@link FillableCell}.
 */
public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
    // Retrieve the cell at the given coordinate
    Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
    // Only FillableCell can be undone
    if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot undo at non-fillable cell: " + coord);
    }
    // Remove any pipe in that cell
    fillable.clearPipe();
    // Roll back the fill-tracking state so that a future fillTiles()
    // will re-compute correctly from the previous state
    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
    prevFilledDistance = null;
    filledTiles.clear();
}
```

### Explanation

- **Type Check**  
  We first look up `cells[coord.row][coord.col]` and ensure it is a `FillableCell`.  If not, we immediately fail with an `IllegalArgumentException`, as per the Javadoc.

- **Clearing the Pipe**  
  The `clearPipe()` method (you should have in your `FillableCell` class) removes any pipe in that cell, effectively making it empty.

- **Resetting Fill State**  
  To ensure that your next call to `fillTiles(int)` recomputes the fill frontier from scratch (and doesn’t incorrectly think tiles are already filled), we:
  1. Record the current size in `prevFilledTiles`.
  2. `prevFilledDistance` is nulled so that distance-based fills restart fresh.
  3. Clear the `filledTiles` set itself.

With this in place, undoing a move properly restores that cell and resets the internal fill bookkeeping.

```java
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;

		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tcell) {
					if (tcell.isSource()) {
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
						}
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source tile must not be on edge");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols
								|| cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into wall or outside map");
						}
						foundSource = tcell;
						this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
					} else {
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
						}
						if (r != 0 && r != rows - 1 && c != 0 && c != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink tile must be on edge");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (adj.row >= 0 && adj.row < rows && adj.col >= 0 && adj.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink points into map");
						}
						foundSink = tcell;
						this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
					}
				} else {
					this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One‑Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One‑Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
			return false;
		}
		if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
			return false;
		}
		fillable.setPipe(p);
		return true;
	}
}
```

I will implement `Map.fillTiles(int distance)` so that it “fills” (marks) every fillable cell reachable along connected pipes up to the given Manhattan‐“pipe‐hops” distance from the source termination cell. We’ll do a simple breadth‑first search (layer by layer), tracking how far we are from the source.

Below is one correct proposal for the full `fillTiles` method (no class wrapper, per request). It:

1. Resets any previous fill state if the requested distance changed (so undo/redo works cleanly).  
2. Performs a BFS starting from `sourceCell.coord`, visiting only cells that are `FillableCell` with a pipe (or the sourceCell itself), and stops at the given distance.  
3. Marks each visited `FillableCell` (and the sink, if reached) by calling its `setFilled()` (via `TerminationCell.setFilled()` for the source).  
4. Remembers how many tiles were filled and what distance was used (for turn‐loss detection elsewhere).

```java
/**
 * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling 
 * distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of 
 * the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
 */
public void fillTiles(int distance) {
    // If distance changed, reset our filled‐tiles tracking
    if (!Objects.equals(prevFilledDistance, distance)) {
        filledTiles.clear();
        prevFilledTiles = 0;
        prevFilledDistance = distance;
    }

    // BFS from the source cell coordinate
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
    // Map each coord to its depth (distance from source)
    Map<Coordinate, Integer> depth = new HashMap<>();

    // Start at the source cell
    Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoord();
    queue.add(start);
    depth.put(start, 0);

    // Ensure the source cell itself is marked filled once
    sourceCell.setFilled();
    filledTiles.add(start);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate coord = queue.poll();
        int d = depth.get(coord);
        if (d >= distance) {
            continue; // we don’t expand beyond requested distance
        }

        // Explore all four directions
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate next = coord.add(dir.getOffset());

            // bounds check
            if (next.row < 0 || next.row >= rows || next.col < 0 || next.col >= cols) {
                continue;
            }

            // skip walls
            Cell c = cells[next.row][next.col];
            if (c instanceof Wall) {
                continue;
            }

            // skip if already visited at an equal or lesser depth
            if (depth.containsKey(next) && depth.get(next) <= d + 1) {
                continue;
            }

            // We only traverse along actual pipes (or into the sink termination)
            boolean isTraversable = false;
            if (c instanceof FillableCell fc) {
                isTraversable = fc.hasPipe();
            } else if (c instanceof TerminationCell tc && !tc.isSource()) {
                isTraversable = true; // allow reaching the sink
            }
            if (!isTraversable) {
                continue;
            }

            // mark depth & enqueue
            depth.put(next, d + 1);
            queue.add(next);

            // mark it filled
            if (c instanceof FillableCell fillable) {
                fillable.setFilled();
            } else if (c instanceof TerminationCell termination) {
                termination.setFilled();
            }
            filledTiles.add(next);
        }
    }

    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
}
```

**Explanation of key points:**

- We reset the `filledTiles` set whenever the requested `distance` changes so that repeated calls with the same distance are incremental but changing distances start fresh.
- We BFS‐expand up to `distance` layers from the source.
- We only enqueue a neighbor if there is a pipe in that neighbor (`FillableCell.hasPipe()`) or if it is the sink tile (`TerminationCell` that isn’t the source).
- Each time we visit a new tile, we call `setFilled()` on it and record its coordinate in `filledTiles`.
- We record `prevFilledTiles` and `prevFilledDistance` to support the turn‐loss logic elsewhere.

This fully completes the requested `fillTiles` method without altering other parts of the class.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {

			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	/**
	 * Creates a map with size of rows x cols. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows  Number of rows.

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {

							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source tiles found");
						}
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source tile must not be on edge");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (adj.row < 0 || adj.row >= rows || adj.col < 0 || adj.col >= cols
								|| cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into wall or outside map");
						}
						foundSource = tcell;
						this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
					} else {
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink tiles found");
						}
						if (r != 0 && r != rows - 1 && c != 0 && c != cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink tile must be on edge");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tcell.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (adj.row >= 0 && adj.row < rows && adj.col >= 0 && adj.col < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink points into map");
						}
						foundSink = tcell;
						this.cells[r][c] = tcell;
					}
				} else {
					this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col). <p> Note: You cannot overwrite the pipe of a cell once the cell is occupied. </p> <p> Hint: Remember to check whether the map coordinates are within bounds, and whether the target cell is a  {@link FillableCell} . </p>
	 * @param row  One‑Based row number to place pipe at.
	 * @param col  One‑Based column number to place pipe at.
	 * @param p    Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return   {@code  true}  if the pipe is placed in the cell,  {@code  false}  otherwise.
	 */
	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
			return false;
		}
		if (fillable.hasPipe()) {
			return false;
		}
		fillable.setPipe(p);
		return true;
	}

	/**
	 * Undoes a step from the map. <p> Effectively replaces the cell with an empty cell in the coordinate specified. </p>
	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .
	 */
	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell fillable)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot undo at non-fillable cell: " + coord);
		}
		fillable.clearPipe();
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
		prevFilledDistance = null;
		filledTiles.clear();
	}
}
```

/**
 * Fills all pipes that are within {@code distance} units from the {@code sourceCell}.
 * 
 * <p>
 * Hint: There are two ways to approach this. You can either iteratively fill the tiles by distance (i.e. filling 
 * distance=0, distance=1, etc), or you can save the tiles you have already filled, and fill all adjacent cells of 
 * the already-filled tiles. Whichever method you choose is up to you, as long as the result is the same.
 * </p>
 *
 * @param distance Distance to fill pipes.
 */
public void fillTiles(int distance) {
    // If distance changed, reset our filled‐tiles tracking
    if (!Objects.equals(prevFilledDistance, distance)) {
        filledTiles.clear();
        prevFilledTiles = 0;
        prevFilledDistance = distance;
    }

    // BFS from the source cell coordinate
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
    // Map each coord to its depth (distance from source)
    Map<Coordinate, Integer> depth = new HashMap<>();

    // Start at the source cell
    Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoord();
    queue.add(start);
    depth.put(start, 0);

    // Ensure the source cell itself is marked filled once
    sourceCell.setFilled();
    filledTiles.add(start);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate coord = queue.poll();
        int d = depth.get(coord);
        if (d >= distance) {
            continue; // we don’t expand beyond requested distance
        }

        // Explore all four directions
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate next = coord.add(dir.getOffset());

            // bounds check
            if (next.row < 0 || next.row >= rows || next.col < 0 || next.col >= cols) {
                continue;
            }

            // skip walls
            Cell c = cells[next.row][next.col];
            if (c instanceof Wall) {
                continue;
            }

            // skip if already visited at an equal or lesser depth
            if (depth.containsKey(next) && depth.get(next) <= d + 1) {
                continue;
            }

            // We only traverse along actual pipes (or into the sink termination)
            boolean isTraversable = false;
            if (c instanceof FillableCell fc) {
                isTraversable = fc.hasPipe();
            } else if (c instanceof TerminationCell tc && !tc.isSource()) {
                isTraversable = true; // allow reaching the sink
            }
            if (!isTraversable) {
                continue;
            }

            // mark depth & enqueue
            depth.put(next, d + 1);
            queue.add(next);

            // mark it filled
            if (c instanceof FillableCell fillable) {
                fillable.setFilled();
            } else if (c instanceof TerminationCell termination) {
                termination.setFilled();
            }
            filledTiles.add(next);
        }
    }

    prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();

I’ll implement `Map.checkPath()` by doing a breadth‑first search from the source cell and seeing whether we can reach the sink cell following only “filled” (i.e. traversable) pipes or the sink itself. Below is one correct, self‑contained implementation of the complete method.

```java
/**
 * Checks whether there exists a path from {@code sourceCell} to {@code sinkCell}.
 *
 * <p>
 * The game is won when the player must place pipes on the map such that a path is formed from the source tile to the sink tile. One of the approaches to check this is to use Breadth First Search to search for the sink tile along the pipes. You may also use other algorithms or create your own, provided it achieves the same goal.
 * The game is lost when no additional pipes are filled in each round after the Nth round. The value of N' can be configured in the loaded map. In the example maps, N` is set to 10.
 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if a path exists, else {@code false}.
 */
public boolean checkPath() {
    // BFS frontier of coordinates to explore
    Queue<Coordinate> queue = new ArrayDeque<>();
    // Track visited positions so we don’t loop forever
    Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();

    // Start from the source cell
    Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoord();
    queue.add(start);
    visited.add(start);

    while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
        Coordinate cur = queue.poll();

        // If we've reached the sink, we're done
        if (cur.equals(sinkCell.getCoord())) {
            return true;
        }

        // Otherwise explore all four directions
        for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
            Coordinate next = cur.add(dir.getOffset());

            // Skip out‑of‑bounds
            if (next.row < 0 || next.row >= rows || next.col < 0 || next.col >= cols) {
                continue;
            }
            if (visited.contains(next)) {
                continue;
            }

            Cell c = cells[next.row][next.col];
            // Only traverse into a cell if it is “filled” pipe or the sink
            boolean canTraverse = false;
            if (c instanceof FillableCell fc && fc.isFilled()) {
                canTraverse = true;
            } else if (c instanceof TerminationCell tc && !tc.isSource() && tc.isFilled()) {
                canTraverse = true;
            }

            if (canTraverse) {
                visited.add(next);
                queue.add(next);
            }
        }
    }

    // Exhausted all possibilities without reaching sink
    return false;
}
```

**Explanation (brief):**  
We perform a standard breadth‑first search starting from the source’s coordinate. We only enqueue adjacent cells that are within bounds, not yet visited, and are “filled” (i.e. pipes already placed or the sink marked filled). If we dequeue the sink’s coordinate, we conclude that a continuous path exists and return true; if the queue empties first, we return false.

```java
	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

			}

			System.out.println();
		}

	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");

		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {

	/**
	 * Creates a map with the given cells. <p> The map should only contain one source tile in any non-edge cell. The map should only contain one sink tile in any edge cell. The source tile must not point into a wall. The sink tile must point outside the map. </p>
	 * @param rows   Number of rows.
	 * @param cols   Number of columns.
	 * @param cells  Cells to fill the map.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map must be at least 3x3");

			throw new IllegalArgumentException("cells.length != rows");

						if (adj.row >= 0 && adj.row < rows && adj.col >= 0 && adj.col < cols) {

				}

		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source tile found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink tile found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;

	 * @param coord  Coordinate to reset.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException  if the cell is not an instance of  {@link FillableCell} .

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {

			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cannot undo at non-fillable cell: " + coord);
		}
		fillable.clearPipe();

		filledTiles.clear();
```
